notes: §1985:X.3.1.2 prints 'PROGRAM-ID. program-name [ IS { COMMON | INITIAL } PROGRAM ] .' with COMMON and INITIAL in choice indicators (one or both, any order, each once). The grammar (programIdParagraph, commonProgramAttribute) parses the attributes in either order with IS and PROGRAM optional; BinderDriver#MakeUnit reads them through ChoiceIndicators#AtMostOnce (a repeat is COBOL2104) and refuses COMMON on an outermost program (COBOL0887, §1985:X.3.1.3 SR3); the 2002 RECURSIVE (COBOL0885) and AS literal (COBOL0900) are refused at 85. Probes at 85: IS COMMON PROGRAM, bare INITIAL, COMMON INITIAL PROGRAM, IS INITIAL COMMON, INITIAL on the outer program all run (an INITIAL program's counter resets on each call, a COMMON one's does not); IS PROGRAM with no attribute, no program-name, a literal name and a missing period are refused. The witness runs an INITIAL COMMON program twice.

next.reason: 1985: 'PROGRAM-ID. program-name [IS {COMMON INITIAL} PROGRAM].' with COMMON and INITIAL in choice indicators. §2023:11.10.2 Format 1 (definition), restated in the program-definition of §2023:10.6.1, keeps COMMON and INITIAL in any order but adds '[AS literal-1]' and the RECURSIVE alternative. No other 1985 rule allows AS or RECURSIVE. Every 1985 paragraph keeps its meaning; more are accepted. CHANGED (looser).
